note.backdrop: A broad rally before the open on Anthropic's pricing. At 8:34 ET the S&P 500 fund was +1.3%, the Nasdaq 100 fund +2.2%, small companies +0.7% and the VIX -9.2%; oil, gold, the dollar and the 10-year yield barely moved. Reuters (on Yahoo) ties it to Anthropic pricing at $83, above its $70-$78 range, with $81 billion raised at about a $1.5 trillion value, and quotes an analyst calling the debut a valuation for the wider AI ecosystem; Anthropic starts trading later today. Traders still price a near-certain 25-basis-point Fed increase in December (LSEG via Reuters). The rally is in AI hardware and its hosts: chips' median +3.2%, circuit-board makers +3.4%, and the 'finance services' group +3.3%, which on inspection is bitcoin miners and crypto treasuries. Health insurers and application software are flat; retailers that rallied Wednesday are slightly down. Only 2 stocks are outside their 9-in-10 range.

read.says: Reuters: Nasdaq futures rose more than 2% after Anthropic priced above its range ($83, $81 billion, about $1.5 trillion); Amazon +2.2% and Alphabet +4.3% premarket as investors in it; Nvidia +1.7% after five straight losses; Intel, AMD, Micron, Marvell +2.7% to +4.3%; CoreWeave and Nebius over +5%, IREN and Applied Digital about +6%; Palo Alto +10.3% with CrowdStrike, Cloudflare, Okta, Zscaler +5-6%; Walmart +0.9% after slightly raising its targets; at 7:18 ET S&P 500 E-minis +1.16%, Nasdaq 100 +2.08%.

Intel +4.65% premarket after its chief executive said it signed a first external customer for its 18A process and expanded its Microsoft partnership with a multi-year Xeon supply deal; the President said the US could allow Nvidia's Blackwell chips to be sold to China in two to three years; Sellas -21% after pricing a $150 million offering at a discount; Palo Alto +10% after beating.

Walmart's quarter: revenue $188.8 billion (+5.2%, 0.8% above consensus), adjusted EPS $0.65 (consensus $0.64), same-store sales +2.9% (4.4% a year earlier), operating margin 4.1% flat; full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised 1.1% to $2.87 at the midpoint.

Williams-Sonoma's third quarter: comparable brand revenue +5.1%, non-GAAP EPS $2.19 (+11.7%); gross margin +150 basis points, of which 140 from IEEPA tariff refunds, with higher oil prices costing 50 in supply chain; fiscal 2026 guidance reiterated, not raised.
Sellas priced 11,538,462 new shares at $13.00 in an underwritten public offering, all sold by the company, about $150 million gross.

Liquidity Services' fiscal fourth quarter: GMV $404.0 million against $404.5 million a year earlier, revenue $106.4 million (-10%) with a shift to consignment, GAAP net income $11.9 million (+52%); fiscal 2027 GMV expected to exceed $2 billion after the Invaluable acquisition.

singles.beneath: On Monday's close, before the trial result, the mosaic put a share-sale filing within 20 sessions at 7.3% against the usual 0.9%, because it had sold shares five times in three years (reported to the person on Nov 18); at Wednesday's close, after the jump, it read 43.2%. The filing came Tuesday and the pricing Wednesday night. Proceeds of $150 million more than double the $134.7 million of cash it held in September. $13.00 is about 28% below Wednesday's $17.95 close and the stock is falling toward it, as Ardent and Vir did. One case is not a record; the mosaic's live calls are scored in research/mosaic_calls.jsonl.

themes.beneath: In proportion: the group has turned three times since Tuesday's close (up after Nvidia's report, down through Wednesday, up again now), each time on a single event. The group is trading events, not a settled view. For the desk's calls from Nov 13's close: Nvidia at $152.75 premarket is 6.2% below $162.89 (line 7.5%); Dell at $325.32 is 5.1% below $342.98 (line 9.5%); AMD at $538.09 is 1.0% above $532.84 (line 9%). All three moved away from their lines overnight.
themes.cause: Anthropic priced at $83, above its range, raising $81 billion (Reuters). Before the open: Coherent +8.3%, Applied Digital +6.4%, CoreWeave +5.6%, IREN +5.0%, Micron +4.6%, Dell +4.5%, Intel +4.4%, Lumentum +4.3%, Marvell +3.9%, Super Micro +3.7%, Vertiv +3.6%, Broadcom +3.0%, AMD +2.4%, Nvidia +1.3%; circuit-board makers Celestica +5.4%, TTM +4.3%, Sanmina +3.8%, Flex +3.5%; its investors Alphabet +3.9% and Amazon +2.6%. Intel also has its own news (a first outside customer for its 18A process, a Microsoft supply deal), and Nvidia its own (the President said Blackwell sales to China could be allowed in two to three years).
themes.mechanism: Anthropic spends what it raises on computing, about $70 billion in the next 12 months by its filings (AP, in the last note); a strong price says that money is there. The sellers of that computing (chips, optics, servers and boards) and its landlords rise with it. The bitcoin miners in the 'finance services' group (Hut 8 +6.3%, TeraWulf +6.1%, Cipher +5.8%, Riot +5.4%, Core Scientific +5.0%) rose four to six times bitcoin's +1.1%; my inference is that the market now prices them as AI data-center landlords, since several have turned their power sites to AI hosting.
themes.name: Anthropic's price lifted AI hardware, its hosts and its investors
themes.watch: Anthropic's first trade: a first price well above $83 confirms the reading; one near or below it would undo this morning. Application software (flat this morning) is the other half of the test.

Williams-Sonoma reported comparable revenue +5.1% and EPS +11.7% but only reiterated its guidance; it is -6.2%. The names that rallied Wednesday are slightly lower: TJX -0.8%, Target -0.7%.
